Chief Executive’s Foreword 
 
Another year is coming to a close and it has been a busy 
and extremely productive year for us in Fingal. There 
have been so many highlights throughout 2025 and 
those which particularly come to mind are in the areas 
of housing provision, improvements to community 
sporting 
facilities, 
economic 
supports 
and 
the 
promotion of arts, culture and heritage within Fingal. We 
have also focussed intently on areas of climate action 
and 
sustainability 
practices, 
building 
transport 
infrastructure for the future and the maintenance of our 
public spaces and shared amenities. The work we carry 
out on behalf of the people of Fingal would not be 
possible without considered financial planning for the 
coming years. A three-year Capital Programme worth 
€1.43 billion was approved at the October monthly 
meeting of the Council paving the way for the 
progression of the 121 current capital projects on site 
and the estimated 309 projects provided for over the 
lifespan of the plan. Not surprisingly, Housing accounts 
for the largest portion of investment with €884m 
allocated while €264m will be spent on Planning and 
Strategic Infrastructure projects. A further €116m is 
earmarked for projects planned by the Economic 
Enterprise 
Tourism 
and 
Cultural 
Development 
Department while €102m will be spent by Environment, 
Climate Action, Active Travel and Sport. This plan 
represents substantial investment in projects spanning 
several council departments which will be of strategic, 
social and economic benefit to the county for many 
years to come.  
On Wednesday, November 19th the budget of €433m for 
2026 was approved at a special meeting of the council. 
The passing of the budget ensures continuity and 
enhancement of service delivery as well as additional 
funding for infrastructure projects in the county. It is 
interesting to note that in 2016 the budget stood at 
€214m meaning that in just 10 years, the allocation for 
essential works and services has more than doubled. 
Certainly, this is testament to the growth of the county 
as a whole and in 2026 the council will spend €1,311 per 
person living in Fingal. Much work has gone into 
balancing the books for the coming year and while 
difficult proposals had to be considered, the resulting 
budget is a robust and manageable financial roadmap 
for the county. I wish to thank the Elected Members for 
their consideration and support of the budget and to the 
Head of Finance and his team for their meticulous work 
over the past months. 
The Chambers Ireland Excellence in Local Government 
Awards were held on Thursday, November 27th. This 
year, Fingal County Council was successfully shortlisted 
for initiatives in categories including Age Friendly, Health 
& Wellbeing, and Supporting Sustainable Communities.  
 
 
We were delighted to accept the award for Meakstown  
Community Centre and Bloom Community Garden in 
the Supporting Sustainable Communities categories. The 
Centre and Garden, which were completely funded by 
the Council, are located in Lanesborough Park in Dublin 
11 and are within a 10-minute walk for the majority of 
residents in the area. Both projects showcase how well-
designed buildings and urban open spaces contribute 
positively to the liveability of our towns and cities. 
Fingal’s gold medal Bloom Garden from 2023 was 
adapted and rebuilt beside the Centre through a 
collaborative effort between local residents, the Council 
and community organisations. The garden has a focus 
on sustainability, with all material used coming from 
council depots that are surplus from other projects and 
perfectly demonstrates the principle of ‘Reduce, Reuse, 
Recycle’. May I offer my congratulations to everyone 
involved with this wonderful project and indeed all the 
entrants to this year’s competition. To be shortlisted in 5 
categories in such prestigious company is something we 
can all be very proud of.   
Following previous successful schemes, it has been 
decided to provide free parking in a number of Pay & 
Display towns across Fingal for three Saturdays in 
December in the run up to Christmas. The towns in 
question are Balbriggan, Rush, Skerries, Swords and in 
Malahide (Bridgefield carpark only). Dates for the free 
parking are 6th, 13th, and 20th of December 2025. This 
initiative endeavours to support businesses in these 
towns by encouraging people to shop local and explore 
some of the artisan Christmas gifts on offer as well as 
soaking up the festive atmosphere in our localities. 
Continuing in that spirit, this year across the county 
there are 44 Christmas trees being erected, with 34 lit 
directly by the Council and the remainder illuminated by 
local community organisations. These stunning trees 
truly add to the excitement of the season as children and 
families look forward to Christmas. 
Finally, as Christmas fast approaches, I would like to 
extend the compliments of the season to you all. May 
you enjoy a peaceful Christmas and a happy and 
prosperous New Year. 
 
Best wishes,  
AnnMarie Farrelly 
Chief Executive

TOURISM DEVELOPMENT 
 
Ireland Home of Halloween 
  
Fingal’s Home of Halloween 2025 delivered a 
highly successful programme of over 25 events 
across the county, blending history, folklore, food, 
arts, and entertainment to create a strong, place-
based festival offer. The campaign achieved 
substantial visibility through coordinated PR, high-
quality photography, real-time content creation, 
and consistently applied branding. New landing 
pages, extensive media coverage, and strong 
stakeholder cooperation contributed to increased 
visitor engagement and a valuable bank of imagery 
and insights for the future years of this festival. The 
initiative has laid a solid foundation for an even 
more strategically focused and locally distinctive 
programme in 2026.

Fingal Tourism Together Sector Symposium  
The second Fingal Tourism Together event of the 
year took place at the Crowne Plaza Hotel, 
Blanchardstown on Wednesday, 5th November. 
This 
half-day 
symposium 
brought 
together 
tourism, food and drink businesses from across 
Fingal to strengthen collaboration and drive 
destination development. It was a comprehensive 
briefing on progress, the implementation of the 
Tourism Strategy and Food and Drink Policy, plans 
for 2026 and Fingal’s ambition to become a leading 
visitor destination.  
 
The programme featured showcase tastings from 
Fingal Food Circle members, presentations, panel 
discussions, and a teaser video for the new 
destination brand, capturing the themes and 
sentiment of Fingal County ahead of the official 
launch in February 2026. The event also provided 
valuable informal networking opportunities and a 
space to shape future collaboration across Fingal’s 
tourism sector.

Seanchaí, Microforest (2020 – 2025)

Through 8 seasons of programming across 5 
years,  Seanchaí Microforest has taken root on the 
grounds of Blakestown Community School. Led by 
artist Gareth Kennedy and created in collaboration 
with over one hundred students, this initiative has 
created a functional, living artwork. Students and 
artists dug, planted, foraged, whittled, explored, 
sketched, cooked, printed, sang, and learned 
deeply throughout this transformative five-year 
journey. Other guest artists working sustainably 
with natural materials shared their practice with 
students during practical workshops. Physically, 
this new growth provides an outdoor learning and 
recreation space for students and the wider school 
community. It encourages human connection and 
creativity while supporting a thriving ecosystem of 
insects, birds and native wild plants, none of which 
were present on the site five years ago. Under the 
stewardship

Blakestown

the 
microforest now rises overhead and provides a

The outer pier (constructed in the 1960s) has 
surpassed its engineering design life and is in a 
progressive state of collapse. Accordingly, this 
section of pier was closed and declared off-limits 
to all during Summer 2025. 
 
Design studies and a preliminary design to 
encapsulate the existing pier and construct a new, 
larger pier around it were completed in 2024. 
Planning Approval for the proposal was granted by 
An Bord Pleanála on 4th September 2024. 
 
The 
Council 
submitted 
an 
application 
for 
Foreshore 
Licences 
to 
the 
Department 
of 
Agriculture, Food & Marine (DAFM) in December 
2024. Two such licences were applied for:- (a) to 
undertake boreholes in the seabed so as to inform 
the engineering design of the foundations 
required for the new pier. This would allow the 
engineering design to be completed, and tenders 
issued to the market to procure contractors for the 
construction of the new pier, AND (b) a licence to 
carry out the construction of the new pier itself. 
These licences are being progressed by DAFM but 
may take up to 18 months meaning it could be 
2027/8 before construction of the new pier can 
commence. 
 
During 2025 and while awaiting licences from 
DAFM, 
extensive 
regular 
inspections 
and 
monitoring of the pier have been on-going. It has 
been observed that the rate of deterioration has 
been rapidly accelerating over the course of the 
year with evidence of increased loss of material 
from within the pier creating a number of cavities 
(some of which are the size of a small car) which 
increases the risk of a sudden collapse of the pier.

Tender documents have been completed and a 
contractor is to be engaged in the coming months 
to fill the cavities with concrete in an effort to stem 
the rate of loss of material from within the pier and 
to slow down the rate of collapse of the pier 
pending the grant of licences from DAFM and the 
construction of the new pier. It is important to be 
aware that this work cannot render the pier safe 
and fit for use. Funding is provided in the Capital 
Budget for these works.

Preventing Homelessness, Notices to Quit and 
Tenant In-situ Acquisitions  
Fingal County Council is aware that households in 
the Fingal area who may have received a notice to 
quit, which is also referred to as a notice of 
termination, from their landlord may be worried or 
unsure of what to do.  
 
Fingal County Council and the Dublin Regional 
Homeless Executive (DRHE) would like to advise 
anyone affected of the services that are available 
to them in these circumstances.  
 
We strongly encourage tenants residing in the 
Fingal area, who have been issued with a notice 
of termination, to contact Fingal County 
Council as soon as they receive a notice from 
their landlord. The contact details for Fingal 
County Council are provided at the bottom of 
this page.  
When the tenants contact Fingal County Council, 
staff in the Housing Department will take note of 
the termination date.  
 
The Council advises the tenant to refer the notice 
to Threshold, a service funded by the DRHE to 
provide a Tenancy Protection Service for private 
renters in the Dublin Region, including Fingal. 
Threshold can also be contacted directly on 
Freephone 1800 454 454 or via their website 
www.threshold.ie 
which 
contains 
more 
information and advice on the validity of your 
notice.  
 
The Council’s first response will be to try to prevent 
homelessness. 
This 
includes 
assessing 
the 
person’s position on the social housing list, 
providing advice on applying for Choice Based 
Lettings, and advising the person on the level of 
Housing Assistance Payment (HAP) they may be 
eligible to receive. 
  
Placement in emergency accommodation will be a 
last resort if no other alternative can be identified.

Agency will then contact the landlord about the 
purchase of the property.

In the pursuit for a fair energy transition, 
metropolitan across Northwest Europe (NWE) face a 
major challenge: the dominance of fossil-fuelled 
private car use has led the transport sector to 
become the largest energy consumer and major 
contributor to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Low 
Emission Zones (LEZs) help reduce pollution, but 
often create conflicting interests between energy, 
housing, and transport policies. 
Against this background, electric carsharing emerges 
as an energy-efficient solution that supports and 
aligns with EU climate and environment goals. The 
STEER-NWE project aims to enable the upscaling of 
electric carsharing through a transnational and 
cross-departmental approach, focused on three 
thematic areas. 
Supported by the use of digital tools and community 
input, STEER-NWE helps local governments create 
inclusive, energy-smart e-carsharing systems.  
The project brings together 11 partners (6 cities and 
5 knowledge and dissemination partners) from 6 
countries (Netherlands, France, Belgium, Ireland, 
Germany, and Luxembourg).

materials, e.g. soil and stones excavated as part of 
developments and then notified as by-product. The

Inspections and/or desktop assessments have been 
completed for 8 of the notifications. Inspections to 
date have found the materials matched what was 
notified under the Article 27 notification with no 
further action required. 
 
The EPA carries out an assessment of all notifications 
and then makes a determination. The determination 
is either to agree with the decision as notified that the 
material is a by-product, or that the material is a 
waste i.e. the notification fails to satisfy the 4 key 
criteria required for the material to be classed as a 
by-product.

Where the EPA makes a determination that the 
material is a waste, and the material has already 
moved, the site of destination becomes an 
unauthorised 
waste 
disposal 
site 
for 
which 
enforcement action is then required. Early inspection 
of sites notified under Article 27 minimises the risk of 
being confronted with an unauthorised waste 
disposal site.
